phrases.text: So welcome back again.
It's time to solve one more problem.
Now in this problem, we are given that a train is two hundred forty meters long.
It passes a man
who is walking at six kilometers per hour
in the opposite direction.
The train takes twelve seconds to completely pass the man.
The question is asking us to find the speed of the train.
Now, the important words here are opposite direction. What does this actually mean?
It means the train and the man are moving towards each other,
so their speeds do not cancel.
Instead,
they get added. This is the basic rule to remember.
When two objects move in opposite directions,
relative speed equals
sum of their speeds.
Now, before using this rule,
we first
need the relative speed.
Why? Because we already know the train length and the time taken to pass the man. When a train passes a person,
the distance covered
is only the length of the train.
So relative speed
equals distance divided by time equals two hundred forty divided by twelve equals twenty meters per second.
Done.
Now we know the relative speed.
The man's speed is given in kilometers per hour.
So let us convert it into meter per second.
Six multiplied by five
divided by eighteen gives us five by three meter per second. Now we can use the relation,
relative speed equals train speed plus man speed.
So twenty equals train speed plus five by three. After simplifying this,
we get train speed equals fifty-five by three meters per second.
Now only one step is left.
The options are in kilometers per hour.
So we convert the speed back.
Fifty-five by three multiplied by eighteen divided by five
gives us sixty-six kilometers per hour.
Hence, the speed of the train is sixty-six kilometer per hour.
So the final answer will be option D.
